predictions.recipe: Files (S3, readable): A = s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/s0400_s0100-01/out/s0100/P_math500.jsonl (step 100, plain); B = s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/base-01/out/F_math500.jsonl (base, cue). In each file keep, per problem_index, the row with the smallest sample value (first in file order on ties). Score every kept row with grader v3 (studies/rlneurons/grader/rln4_grader_v3.py) from its text and gold; an empty extraction scores 0. S = problem_index values that have a kept row in both files with cap_hit false in both. err(X) = (number of S rows of X with v3 score 0) / |S|. Statistic = err(A) - err(B). Cap-hit rows are excluded through S; problems missing from either file are excluded.
predictions.note: Files: A = s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/s0400_s0100-01/out/s0100/P_math500.jsonl (500 rows, 1 per problem, sample 0), B = .../r3/base-01/out/F_math500.jsonl (500 rows), fetched to runs/theory-tests/r3/... Kept row = smallest sample, first in file order on ties (all samples are 0, so no ties matter). Score = rln4_lib.grade_v3(gold, text)['score_v3'] (the function rln4_grader_v3.py calls); extracted_v3 None or blank scores 0. S = both kept, cap_hit false in both (cap_hit false always coincides with finish_reason 'stop' in these files). Statistic = err(A) - err(B) over S, bootstrap over problems as (scoreA, scoreB) pairs. B's text starts with the prefilled cue ' line!\n\nOkay' (included in text); A has no prefill. alt_measured: unpaired reading, each file's error rate over its own cap_hit-false rows. Risk: grader v3 judgment errors (flip review lists a few) apply to both files alike.

predictions.experiment: Cause: whose deliberative length step 100 has. Median per-problem log ratio of step-100 finished length to the cued base's finished length, same problems. This mechanism (step 100 has the cued base's length) predicts about 0.05. A rival in which the first 100 steps already install RL's final long-answer mode predicts about step 2,800's ratio to the cued base, about 0.6.
predictions.recipe: Files A and B and the kept rows and paired set S exactly as in the first recipe (one row per problem_index, smallest sample; S = problems with cap_hit false in both files). For each problem in S compute ln(max(n_new_A, 1) / max(n_new_B, 1)). Statistic = median over S (for an even count, the mean of the two middle values). No grading is needed. Cap hits and missing problems are excluded through S.
predictions.note: Same files, kept rows and S as k=1. Statistic = median over S of ln(max(n_new_A,1)/max(n_new_B,1)), even count = mean of the two middle values; bootstrap over (n_new_A, n_new_B) pairs. Ambiguity: whether B's n_new includes the 3 prefilled cue tokens is not stated in the rows (prefill_ids holds them separately; n_generated = n_new + 1 in the rows seen); main uses n_new as written. alt_measured uses n_generated in place of n_new. A 3-token difference is negligible at these lengths.

predictions.experiment: Case where an effect should not appear: the opening cue's value at step 100. On the base the cue is worth many points; if step 100 already writes the cue's opening by itself, prefilling the cue adds nothing. Accuracy of step 100 with the cue minus step 100 plain, all 500 problems, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95.
predictions.recipe: Files: A = s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/s0400_s0100-01/out/s0100/P_math500.jsonl (plain) and D = s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/s0400_s0100-01/out/s0100/F_math500.jsonl (cue). In each file keep, per problem_index, the row with the smallest sample value (first in file order on ties). Score each kept row with grader v3 (studies/rlneurons/grader/rln4_grader_v3.py) from text and gold; a row with cap_hit true counts 0 whatever v3 gives; an empty extraction counts 0. Keep problems present in both files. Statistic = mean score over D minus mean score over A on those problems.
predictions.note: Files: A = .../r3/s0400_s0100-01/out/s0100/P_math500.jsonl (500 rows), D = .../r3/s0400_s0100-01/out/s0100/F_math500.jsonl (only 420 rows, 420 problems, 1 each). Score: cap_hit true -> 0, else grade_v3 score_v3 with empty extraction -> 0. Main = mean over D minus mean over A on the problems present in both (at most 420, not the 'all 500' of the experiment text). alt_measured: the 'all 500' reading as each file's mean over all of its own kept rows, unpaired (D 420, A 500). Risk: the 80 problems missing from D may not be a random subset (e.g. a job cut short in index or length order), which could bias both readings relative to a full-500 comparison.
